events/1313_impero/phases/0/transitionTe: At the lectern, Boccaccio unrolls copies of three letters.
events/1313_impero/phases/0/announcement: Boccaccio: “The last political gamble of his life. He put everything he had — including any chance of going home — on one German. Watch how he places the bet.”
events/1313_impero/phases/1/narrative: Henry VII leads his army over the Alps. On the exile’s desk three open letters are written, one after another, and left lying there.
events/1313_impero/phases/1/instruction: Read all three letters, then hear what the scribe says.
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/0/name: Letter 1 · To the princes of Italy
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/0/dialo: To the Kings and Princes of Italy
“Look, now is the time of grace! The bridegroom is coming. Bride of Italy, dry your tears — the Emperor of Rome comes to bring peace to all peoples!”
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/1/dialo: “You fools! You trample every law of God and man, greed drives you to every kind of wrong — your walls will not save you. Under the eagle you will tremble!”
(the pen does not stop) That felt good. It also nails me to the exile list for good.
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/2/dialo: “Why do you delay? You winter in Milan and think Tuscany is nothing to worry about? Wrong! Strike Florence first — that viper, that sick sheep, poisoning the whole flock!”
events/1313_impero/phases/1/npcs/3/dialo: (his hand shaking) Sir, these letters… the city you are cursing is your own.
Once they go out and every city has read them — Florence will never, never pardon you.
events/1313_impero/phases/2/narrative: The scribe holds the letters and waits for the last word.
events/1313_impero/phases/2/question: Do the three letters go out?
events/1313_impero/phases/2/options/0/re: He did not wait. History does not offer that option — the man in front of you never left himself a way back.
events/1313_impero/phases/2/options/1/re:
Justice turns on this one throw.
Send them — let all Italy hear.
events/1313_impero/phases/2/conclusion/n: The three letters travel all over Italy. Florence answers by shutting Dante out of every pardon, for ever. He staked the road home on a dream of empire.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/travelNarrat: Henry VII crosses the Alps and comes south. Stop by stop, the fever cools.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/instruction: Follow the eagle’s route. Click each stop.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/0/: In Sant’Ambrogio, Henry puts on the iron crown of Lombardy. In the watching crowd an exiled poet pushes to the front — bends down, and kisses the Emperor’s feet.
I saw him. Justice in the flesh, alive. Twenty years — and this is the first time I have felt so close to home.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/1/: Brescia shuts its gates and holds out. Four months of siege, disease everywhere, and the allied army begins to fall apart. The Guelf cities watch coldly — King Robert of Naples is already gathering troops.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/2/: Street fighting in Rome. The enemy holds St Peter’s, so the crowning has to move to the Lateran — half a coronation. The Pope is far away in Avignon, and even his envoys are just going through the motions.
The crown is on, but the doors of St Peter’s are shut. …A bad sign.
events/1313_impero/phases/3/waypoints/3/: The army marches south again. On 24 August, in a small town near Siena called Buonconvento —
events/1313_impero/phases/4/transitionTe:
Before the bier, the eagle banner is furled.
After Henry died, Dante never hoped for anything from the politics of this world again.
He wrote the Emperor into the Paradiso.

At the lectern, Boccaccio is quiet for a long time.
events/1313_impero/phases/4/announcement: Boccaccio: “He lost the bet. But listen — it was because the throne on earth stood empty that he built the whole of Heaven into a courtroom. The verdicts of the Divine Comedy last longer than any emperor’s.”
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/question: In 1310–1313, who did Dante stake his last political hopes on?
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/options/2: Henry VII, the Holy Roman Emperor
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/0/explanation: When Henry VII came south into Italy, Dante wrote open letter after open letter: telling the princes to go and meet him, cursing Florence, pushing Henry to attack Florence first — so savagely that he destroyed any chance of ever being pardoned. In 1313 Henry fell ill and died at Buonconvento, and the dream was over.
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/1/question: What image did Dante use against the Church’s “sun and moon” argument, to say that empire and Church stand side by side?
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/1/explanation: The Church taught the “sun and moon” doctrine: imperial power is the moon, and can only borrow its light from the papal sun. Dante answered with “two suns” (the image is in Purgatorio XVI): empire and Church each take their authority straight from God. The Monarchia argues the whole case; the Church later banned it and burned it.
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/2/question:
Paradiso XXX, among the seats of the highest rose:
“One chair stands empty, with a ___ laid on it, waiting for the great Henry”
quiz/1313_impero/quizzes/2/explanation: Paradiso XXX: Beatrice points out to Dante the empty seat and the crown in the rose of Heaven — the emperor earth had no room for has a place kept for him there.
